q: In the eight-step turn, what happens after response parsing when the model's output contains tool calls?
options: Memory update
Response delivery
Tool execution
Context assembly
explanation: Tool calls route to execution, then a follow-up model call; text-only output skips ahead. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §4.1)

q: The model generates a call to a tool the agent does not have. What normally happens?
options: Validation rejects it and returns an error to the model, which usually acknowledges the missing tool
The runtime crashes
A similarly named tool runs instead
The call is dropped with no feedback
explanation: Hallucinated tools fail the existence and schema checks and come back as recoverable errors. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §4.3)

q: Which of these does tool call validation NOT check?
options: Whether the tool is in the enabled list
Whether the operation's outcome matches the user's intent
Whether arguments match the input schema
Whether the tool has hit its rate limit
explanation: Validation covers format and tier; intent alignment is left to SOUL.md and AGENTS.md. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §4.3)

q: Why does the book suggest routing the end-of-session summary to Haiku?
options: Haiku has a larger context window
AGENTS.md requires it
Sonnet cannot write files
Summarizing a session is structured extraction, not complex reasoning, so a cheaper model suffices
explanation: The summary is an extra model call; a cheaper model handles it well at a fraction of the cost. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §4.4)

q: A user talks to the agent on Telegram for personal matters and on Slack for work. How are sessions handled by default?
options: One session shared across all channels
One session per channel shared by all users
Separate sessions per channel and per peer
One session for every interaction
explanation: The default isolation key is channel plus peer, which avoids context bleed. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §4.5)

q: What distinguishes summarization from truncation as session pruning strategies?
options: Truncation keeps continuity; summarization drops turns
Summarization compresses the oldest turns into a summary; truncation drops them with no summary
They behave identically
Summarization only applies to heartbeat sessions
explanation: Summarization preserves continuity at some cost; truncation is cheaper but loses it. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §4.5)

q: An operator disables the heartbeat to save money, and the next morning's scheduled briefing never arrives. Why?
options: Scheduled and time-triggered work depends on the heartbeat; without it the agent acts only on user messages
The briefing requires Opus
The Telegram token expired
MEMORY.md crossed its hard threshold
explanation: The book warns to disable heartbeats only when there are no scheduled tasks or background processing. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §4.6)

q: Cache hit rate collapsed right after an operator put a current timestamp at the top of the system context. Why?
options: Timestamps overflow the context window
Caching is disabled for Telegram
Timestamps trigger session pruning
A changing token at the start invalidates the cache for everything after it
explanation: Cache hits require identical tokens in the same positions, so volatile content must come last. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §4.7.3)

q: An agent forgets an interaction even though its reply looked normal. Logs show disk quota exceeded under memory/. What is the right fix?
options: Switch to Opus
Monitor workspace disk, alert at 80%, and rotate memory logs
Increase maxQueueDepth
Enable streaming
explanation: Memory write failures are silent to the user, so disk monitoring and log rotation prevent them. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §4.7.4)

q: An operator edits AGENTS.md during an active session, and the agent ignores the new rule. What is the cause?
options: AGENTS.md has a size limit
Rules must be written to MEMORY.md
Identity files load at session start, so the session must restart
The event queue is full
explanation: Compare the file modification time with the loaded_at time; if newer, restart the session. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §4.11)
